title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. G is GL2, viewed as a group scheme over a base ring A0 (or a scheme S); PG is the projective group PGL2. ρ and σ are two regular sections of G. The previous page introduced ε̃0 = σ̃^{-1}ρ̃ and ε̃1 = ρ̃σ̃^{-1} in PG, related by ε̃1 = ρ̃(ε̃0) = σ̃(ε̃0) (conjugation). It lifted them to ε0 = -σ^{-1}ρ and ε1 = -ρσ^{-1} in SG. It then required ε0 and ε1 to be unipotent in every fibre, writing εi = 1 + Ni.

The page.
1. The page opens by requiring that N0 and N1 be nowhere homothetic, i.e. independent in every fibre.
2. Under this condition, the two unipotent elements give the intersection of their two Borels (a maximal torus) together with nonzero vectors in opposite root groups. Grothendieck says that ε̃0, ε̃1 (with the torus ε̃0(G_a)-type data) 'définissent un épinglage canonique de PG dans des G'. In SGA3 language this is a canonical pinning.
3. In pinned coordinates he writes (26): ρ = [[0,u],[v,w]] and σ = [[0,u'],[v',w']], with u, v, u', v' invertible and w, w' arbitrary functions.
4. He computes (27):
   - -σ^{-1}ρ = [[-v/v', (uw'-wu')/(u'v')],[0,-u/u']]
   - -ρσ^{-1} = [[-u/u', 0],[(vw'-wv')/(u'v'), -v/v']]
   I checked both formulas directly; they are correct.
5. The pinning normalisation is ε0 = [[1,*],[0,1]] and ε1 = [[1,0],[1,1]]. This forces (28): u' = -u and v' = -v.
6. Then -ρσ^{-1} = [[1,0],[(w+w')/u,1]], so (29): w + w' = u.
7. Equivalently (30): ρ + σ = uP, where P = diag(0,1) is the elementary projector attached to the pinning. This determines σ from ρ and P.
8. Finally (31): ε0 = [[1,u/v],[0,1]] and N0 = [[0,u/v],[0,0]].

Purpose. This is a normal form for pairs of 2×2 matrices whose 'quotients' σ^{-1}ρ and ρσ^{-1} are, up to sign, transverse regular unipotents. In other words, it is a family version of normalising two parabolic elements with distinct fixed points. It serves the 'équation des lacets' study of GL2/PGL2-valued solutions, i.e. representations of fundamental groups of P^1 minus points with unipotent local monodromy.

The next page turns this into intrinsic numerical criteria: det σ = det ρ, det(σ+ρ) = 0, and Tr(σ+ρ) invertible, with u = Tr(σ+ρ) and P = (σ+ρ)/u.
errors: (29): the manuscript appears to write 'i.e. w' = w - u'; from w' + w = u it should read w' = u - w. This is a harmless slip: (30) and (31) are computed correctly from w + w' = u.

The off-diagonal entry of the target ε0 in (27) is left undetermined (overwritten '?'); (31) later shows it equals u/v, so ε0 is not normalised to [[1,1],[0,1]], only ε1 is. This is consistent but should be noted.

ideas.what: Two transverse regular unipotent elements of PGL2 over a base determine a canonical pinning (épinglage)
ideas.modern_name: pinning / épinglage of a reductive group scheme; normal form for a pair of parabolics with distinct fixed points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Demazure–Grothendieck, SGA3 (épinglages); classical for parabolic pairs in SL2
ideas.where_published: SGA3 (notion of épinglage); this specific application is unpublished

ideas.what: Normal form ρ + σ = uP (u invertible scalar, P rank-one elementary projector) characterising pairs with -σ^{-1}ρ and -ρσ^{-1} transverse unipotent
ideas.modern_name: explicit parametrisation of pairs of matrices with prescribed parabolic products (relative character-variety computation)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore linear algebra (character varieties of free groups / Fricke coordinates)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine explicit 2×2 matrix computation over a general base, putting a pair of transverse unipotents into pinned normal form. It is correct (apart from a sign slip) and is a step toward the intrinsic criteria on the next page. There is nothing beyond standard linear algebra and SGA3-style pinnings.
transcription_corrections: 'épi-gluf(s)' should read 'épinglage(s)' (pinning) throughout: 'définissent un épinglage canonique de PG dans des G', 'puisque … est épinglage', 'par définition des notions épinglage', 'projection élém. associée à l'épinglage envisagé'.
'w,w' ∈ Γ G_0' is most likely 'w,w' ∈ Γ(G_a)' (arbitrary functions), while u, v, u', v' ∈ Γ(G_m) are invertible.
Line 2: 'ε̃0 ∈ Γ ε̃0(G_{10})' is unclear; the G-subscripts are likely G_m / G_a-type tori and subgroups, not 'G_10'.
The '?' entry of the target ε0 in (27) is an overwritten digit (possibly 1 or 2), left as undetermined.
(29) reads 'w' + w = u, i.e. w' = w - u' in the manuscript (a slip for u - w).
